historical_c5_descriptive_comparison.scope: Historicalc5 comparison is descriptive, not an isolated speedup estimate: different allocations,4 versus8 requested CPUs, preprocessing implementation and instrumentation; actual historical trainer CPU affinity was not recorded. Use separately repeated matched controls for causal performance evidence.

independent_cpu_allocator_diagnostic.finding: End-only malloc_trim released resident pages while live cache fingerprints/counters and glibc allocated bytes remained unchanged in this CPU replay. GC alone did not explain the resident growth.
limitations: Separate CPU replay, not intervention in training; decoder/thread allocation timing differs from concurrent GPU training.
mallinfo2 describes glibc allocation arenas/mmap bookkeeping; it does not prove Python reachability or attribute every native allocator.
Garbage collection and malloc_trim are invoked only after all1000rows with live caches retained and fingerprinted unchanged.
RSS/PSS excludes unmapped filesystem page cache; observed allocator release does not establish a general leak fix.

This replay worker reported2threads; live training workers reported32. Native allocation/thread timing differs, so the replay does not prove all training growth shares this cause or qualify a production trim policy.
Single training seed42 and256teacher-forced diagnostic rows; no free-generation or full-held-out release qualification.
NF4 andBF16 training overlap on different accelerator nodes. Frozen then trained scoring is sequential within each arm; filesystem/cache state is uncontrolled.
Sampled NVML and process memory peaks are observed lower bounds; report sampling gaps and null missing measurements, never truepeak claims.
1GiB cache cap excludes workers, pending rows, decoder temporaries and allocator residency. Process RSS/PSS/HWM excludes unmapped filesystem pagecache.
Phase records describe intervals ending at each event. checkpoint_begin flushes preceding work; only checkpoint_complete covers checkpoint-write interval.
Native child loading is instrumented; orchestration setup before sampler initialization lacks equivalent external memory coverage.

Host kernel driver and native mappedlibcuda filename versions were observed separately; theCPU-only diagnostic nvidia-smi device query was unavailable, so accelerator SKU/memory come from the actual native GPU preflight.
Oldbuild performance comparison is descriptive. Independent cross-build checkpoint equality is reported separately by its dedicated audit.

original_device_process_memory_criterion.scope: Original design criterion concerns maximum device-process memory for each paired seed. Allocator peaks are a separate optimization filter; sampled process peaks are lower bounds and do not establish unsampled truepeak differences or the required3seed result.

worker_memory_observation.finding: Worker anonymous memory grew during training despite the bounded1GiB cache; trainer PSS remained comparatively stable. No unbounded framework window/future/cache reference history was identified in read-only audit. A separate CPU replay demonstrates freed glibc page retention; attribution of all live-training growth remains unresolved.
worker_memory_observation.scope: Worker identity comes from one read-only live process classification. Milestones use the last matching worker sample within5seconds before each native update boundary; they are sampled observations, not exact boundary values or truepeaks. No intervention in training; the separate CPU allocator diagnostic is independent evidence.
